description: Explicit maintainer editorial selection from unified Experts comparisons. Registration is distinct from participant authorization and independent validation; builds do not select or approve evidence automatically.

publication.title: Exact monetary meaning does not require a universal currency-wide calculation scale
publication.limits: The paper’s common quantum is an application architecture. Applying it everywhere could reduce exact intermediate values prematurely. The reviewer did not validate its equations or worked financial calculations.

publication.title: Idempotent request identity includes content and an explicitly bounded effect
publication.limits: Reviewer scenario: a lost response leads to retrying with the same key but a changed amount. Treating this as the same financial instruction can suppress a legitimate change or misidentify the result. Atomic key storage is the paper’s design; a key alone does not coordinate every external effect.

publication.title: Monitoring evidence is not an eligible business approval
publication.limits: A product can combine these controls in one interface, but their evidentiary questions differ. The review is a synthesis, not a causal test of any particular approval implementation.

publication.title: Balanced totals do not establish the validity of an economic event
publication.limits: The paper explicitly notes balanced errors but cites Ellerman; the original cited account has not been checked. A reviewer-created duplicate posting can preserve totals, but is not a Core operation or a financial test executed here.

publication.title: Non-significance is not permission to remove a mandatory control
publication.limits: The source’s literal “does not affect” wording is stronger than its observational evidence warrants. Failure to cross a significance threshold is not an equivalence test. Positive results in EVD-0006 concern different settings and do not directly refute this study.

publication.title: Fast responses do not establish that the relevant facts are current
publication.limits: The source reports synchronization issues, not a measured stale-snapshot control failure. The financial scenario in the original finding is reviewer-created. Historical reports may intentionally use old observations.

publication.title: Timestamp precedence cannot replace the defined aggregation of effective approvals
publication.limits: The example assumes both opposing Decisions are valid and still effective. Legitimate withdrawal/supersession differs from timestamp overwrite. LWW may still suit a cache or application value whose declared semantics permit it.

publication.title: A changed prediction is a changed fact basis, not necessarily nondeterministic condition evaluation
publication.limits: Reviewer scenario: a later model recomputes a different risk estimate; this does not reproduce the earlier supplied estimate. Whether that estimate is material and retained depends on the declared policy.

publication.title: Authorize the action that is actually executed
publication.limits: Binding a human decision to the executed parameters is the reviewer’s application-level inference. The inspected architecture does not prove freedom from time-of-check/time-of-use faults. Not every FinKore action requires a human signature.

publication.title: Observed input still needs the applicable business validation
publication.limits: This transfer is reviewer inference, not a rule formulated by the authors for FinKore. A sensor’s inventory observation alone does not establish a sale. Cleaning data must not silently invent business facts.

publication.title: Successful import does not authenticate a complete historical record
publication.limits: A post-migration consistency check can find violated relations but is limited by the predicates and data it covers. Source authentication, omitted history and external reconciliation are separate application responsibilities.

publication.title: Historical reconstruction and recalculation under a new policy differ
publication.limits: The broader calculation discussion is reviewer inference. Current Workflow requirements prevent silent rebinding; they do not define an execution engine for all historical financial calculations. Regulatory claims were not independently checked.

publication.title: Counting controls does not establish independent assurance
publication.limits: The shared-input example is reviewer inference. Correlation modeling in the abstract motivates the question; it does not quantify FinKore risk or prove a universal optimal control policy. A risk model does not waive an applicable MUST.

publication.title: Locally valid states do not imply a global serial order
publication.limits: A global serial order is not required for every application. The source intentionally offers weaker isolation with potential throughput benefits; this is not a hidden defect. Financial implications depend on the composing policy.

publication.title: Passing a finite suite has a defined evidential scope
publication.limits: The passage concerns ACID benchmark testing; applying the epistemic limit to FinKore is reviewer inference. Strong cases remain useful. The source’s benchmark requirements do not become FinKore requirements.

publication.title: Changing the representation does not establish equivalent control
publication.limits: The transfer to FinKore is reviewer inference. The article’s legal assertions, Just-In-Time process and document package are not verified as current or universal. A syntactically valid message does not itself establish payment eligibility.

publication.title: A correlated score is not an independent conformity test
publication.limits: Applying this study to FinKore is reviewer inference. The study does not discredit all ESG measurement or ML, nor demonstrate an actual FinKore violation. Shared measurement processes can explain correlations; alternative model-design explanations remain possible.

publication.title: Producer idempotence does not settle application-effect uniqueness
publication.limits: The crash-after-effect-before-acknowledgement scenario is reviewer inference. Broker guarantees have a useful defined scope. Application deduplication still needs defined keys, retention, durable recovery and a consistent effect boundary; the abstract does not establish those details.

publication.title: Preventing an invalid state does not guarantee eventual completion
publication.limits: This is methodological transfer from healthcare, not a financial rule demonstrated by that study. Fairness, resource availability and admissible requests matter. An intentionally terminal state is not a deadlock defect; statistical confidence is not an unconditional proof for arbitrary executions.

publication.title: A proof can establish a property different from the intended rule
publication.limits: A changed ordering example is reviewer inference; the source reports a particular assistant/model interaction. No general LLM error rate or superiority of a prompting strategy is established here. Formulas and figures were not independently inspected visually.

publication.title: Snapshot coherence and freshness are separate properties
publication.limits: These financial scenarios are reviewer inferences. A consistent snapshot can be appropriate within an application’s bound. TxCache does not remove the database’s anomalies or establish universal safe staleness for financial authorization.

publication.title: Preserving collected traces does not prove capture of required events
publication.limits: A separate expected workload can test coverage if it is independent of the collector. This is not a mandate to record every request or collect sensitive content indiscriminately. A diagnostic retry trace is not itself a unique financial effect.

publication.title: Convergence does not by itself promise permanence after a response
publication.limits: An external action triggered by a later-discarded result is reviewer inference. A clearly provisional response may be appropriate. The source explicitly acknowledges the limitation; this review does not declare its framework generally unsuitable or its proofs invalid.

publication.title: Preserve the magnitude of a financial value; do not silently truncate it
publication.limits: This is a personal recollection, not a verified experiment or a universal statement about COBOL. No details from the withheld follow-up are used. Exact representability does not define universal database field capacity. The Open Questions in spec/money/representation.md leave portable precision, scale and overflow limits unresolved: this behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core. Unsupported amounts already have a portable failure category; this comparison does not set the capacity threshold or introduce an overflow code.

publication.title: Treat overlooked exceptions as failure cases worth making observable
publication.limits: The surrounding prediction about the first day of go-live is personal rhetoric, not a measured rate or universal temporal claim. Only failures already defined by the owning specification can acquire expected observations; a test suite must not invent banking exceptions or imply exhaustive correctness.

publication.title: A deployment rollback plan and a rejected-operation guarantee have different boundaries
publication.limits: The interviewee frames this as advice, not a reported deployment protocol or proof of atomic recovery. Deployment rollback, external compensation, restoration of a committed action and local non-mutation on rejection are distinct. FinKore does not supply a rollback engine, distributed transaction protocol, migration workflow, or concrete reversal accounting effects.

publication.title: Stable portable failures and actionable diagnostics serve different readers
publication.limits: The quote is advice supported by a personal incident, not a FinKore requirement for log content, manuals, localized wording, or an error envelope. SPEC-ERROR-003 permits messages and context (MAY); entity paths and stable violation identifiers are SHOULD obligations. Sensitive financial, personal and implementation data are not automatically safe to include.

publication.title: Validate supplied financial observations without confusing validity with factual truth
publication.limits: Product-specific names, address formats and numeric-field rules must be declared by a composing domain. The anecdote supplies no universal input grammar or guarantee that a validator detects fraud, missing facts, or all bad assumptions. FinKore validates declared conditions against supplied observations; it does not certify their real-world truth.

publication.title: Retrying a batch is not evidence that each economic effect occurs only once
publication.limits: This is a reported operational tendency, not proof that every retry duplicates payments. A retry after an uncertain outcome, a domain rejection and a new economic instruction are different cases. Concrete payment posting, batch scheduling, reconciliation and distributed effect coordination are outside the current Core contract. No idempotency key scheme, retention period or payment operation is prescribed.

publication.title: Batch dependencies expose a distinction between reproducible facts and fresh facts
publication.limits: The source supplies no quantitative freshness bound or dependency protocol. WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 does not require always-latest data; ENTITY-IMPORT-007 compares expected values to the supplied observation, not to an independently queried remote system. The interview's suggestion that real-time processing removes these problems is not generalized: distributed real-time systems still require dependency and freshness policies.

publication.title: Preserve financial meaning while changing implementation technology
publication.limits: This is practitioner experience, not a demonstrated equivalence proof or a prescribed migration architecture. CORE-005.3 addresses reproducibility from the same declared inputs, state and context; it does not by itself prove equivalence between an old and a new implementation. MONEY-REPRESENTATION-006 covers Money only. SPEC-COMPATIBILITY-012 classifies changes to the published FinKore contract, not every consumer deployment. The interview does not authorize workflow migration, a universal COBOL-to-Java transformation, AI extraction guarantees, new portable errors, or recovery of undocumented rules by inference.

publication.title: Keep institution-specific business rules explicit rather than treating one practice as universal
publication.limits: The account does not establish the content or legal validity of any current regulation, nor does it turn a bank-specific rule into FinKore Core. The 1990 Collor Plan and printed-report story are not reconstructed as portable account-freeze or regulator-submission operations. CORE-002.2 governs financial-change validation, not a jurisdictional policy catalog. ENTITY-VALIDATION-001 requires applicable rules to hold without selecting the business rules for every bank, product or country.

publication.title: Validate generated implementations against explicit financial obligations
publication.limits: The quotation concerns developers reviewing generated code; CoreDoc concerns financial evaluations. Their relationship is contextual, not an assertion that CORE-005.3 mandates a developer qualification, AI review process or source-extraction method. SPEC-CONFORMANCE-001 and -002 apply regardless of how code is produced. SHOULD exceptions remain documented recommendations, not automatically mandatory rules. No interview, generated program, repository artifact check or finite test set proves external implementation conformance; consumers own implementation validation and execution evidence.

Allocation path only. Amount and currency are retained, but largest-fraction recipient selection differs from Core declared-order distribution. BCMath intermediates and float ranking were not executed or exhaustively verified.
publication.title: Money PHP — Allocation rules

publication.limits: FloorToFirst strategy, positive integer weights and a fixed context with explicitly matched scale/step. Other strategies, rational/zero-weight inputs and Brick Math internals are not claimed equivalent to Core.
publication.title: Brick Money — Ordered allocation in explicit integer steps

publication.limits: A numeric helper, not a complete Money operation: currency construction is outside the reading. Successive division, numeric types and decimal cutoff affect the result; all-zero weights are replaced with equal weights.
publication.title: RubyMoney — Allocation carries residual value through successive splits

publication.limits: The inspected Money/BigMoney addition path checks currencies. Full ordering, equality, conversion and provider semantics were not assessed. Native exceptions are not portable FinKore error codes.
publication.title: Joda-Money — Money addition checks currency before combining amounts

publication.limits: The safe API and selected number-backend utility were read. Remainder goes to larger weights; zero ratios and scale derivation differ from Core. The no-progress guard is not proof of exact conservation beyond safe number precision.
publication.title: Dinero.js — Allocation prioritizes larger weights for residual units

publication.limits: Signed equal splitting and ratio allocation were read. Equal splitting preserves signed residuals in the selected cases; an all-zero ratio list can return zero amounts for a nonzero source. Fixed-width overflow limits remain unverified.
publication.title: GoMoney — Signed splitting preserves residual units, except the zero-weight fallback

publication.limits: Constructor and rounding/context paths only. A missing context can select an ambient policy; standard rounding normally derives scale from currency. An expressly declared composing-domain policy is a separate assessment.
publication.title: NodaMoney — Context-selected rounding can change a value at construction

publication.limits: Addition/subtraction and selected equality/context observations only. Decimal representation alone does not establish unrestricted exactness; native numeric-zero conveniences and equality semantics differ from the portable boundary.
publication.title: py-moneyed — Addition is currency-checked, but numeric context remains observable

publication.limits: A ledger balance-assertion policy, outside current Core ledger/reconciliation scope. Its decimal tolerance does not redefine exact Money equality or authorize approximate monetary conformance checks.
publication.title: Beancount — Balance assertions use a separate decimal tolerance policy

publication.limits: Actual/360 time fractions and endpoint inclusion only. Interest accrual is outside current Core; Time test tolerances are not exact Money comparison rules. Date internals and a complete interest calculation were not verified.
publication.title: QuantLib — Interest year fractions depend on day-count and endpoint policy

publication.limits: ACH file/batch control validation, not current Core payment semantics or a certification against a Nacha edition. Selected totals checks and assertions do not prove all variants, bounds or settlement behavior.
publication.title: Moov ACH — Payment control totals are checked at file and batch levels

publication.limits: Constructing inverse postings is not persisted reversal. Original-event linkage, one-time eligibility, authorization and committed history were not established. Amount pointers are shallow-copied, so deep ownership is not proven.
publication.title: Formance Ledger — Reversal swaps posting direction and reverses posting order

publication.limits: Configured account constraints on the normal new-transfer path. Pending/posted counters and pre-insertion guards were read; consensus, persistence atomicity and post/void paths were not audited. Ledger/reservation semantics remain outside Core.
publication.title: TigerBeetle — Pending debits consume a configured posted-credit budget

publication.limits: Invoice/payment domain context, outside current Core. Selected tests assert aggregate rejection and unchanged invoice outstanding, but were not run. Fresh database reads alone do not establish a race-free validation/commit boundary.
publication.title: ERPNext — Payment allocation is checked against fresh aggregate outstanding amounts
Completion has meaning within a declared scope
publication.limits: The account does not define FinKore transitions or universal payment-finality criteria. Settlement remains outside the Core scope.

publication.title: Relevant conditions must be checked before a result becomes observable
publication.limits: The amount and channel policy belongs to the product. The technical cause and prior existence of the rule were not verified by inspecting the system.

publication.title: Later recovery does not replace preservation on rejection
publication.limits: No FinKore rejection or violation was established. The rule does not guarantee distributed atomicity or generic handling of communication failures.

publication.title: Identity connects evidence and distinguishes operations
publication.limits: The bank identifier model was not examined. Entity and Audit Event identities do not establish economic deduplication or an idempotency protocol.

publication.title: Distinct evolution needs declared meaning and a link to the earlier fact
publication.limits: Institutional terms do not automatically map to Correction, Reversal, Void or Supersession. The Core does not define concrete accounting postings.

publication.title: An adjustment needs to remain linked to its original
publication.limits: The answer does not establish additional identifiers or a portable immutable relationship. Free text evidences the need; it does not demonstrate that every requirement was implemented.

publication.title: Approval has an identifiable subject and financial content
publication.limits: Eligibility policy and the subject model were not examined. The account does not determine per-item approval, quorum or a universal chain. Answer 16 concerns entries already processed and does not document changes between approval and execution. It does not demonstrate revalidation after facts change or immutable preservation of the complete decision.

publication.title: Attribution supports reconstruction of requests and authorizations
publication.limits: The answer does not demonstrate every portable field, stable identities or immutable history. Automated execution must not be attributed by inference to the human approver.

publication.title: Evaluations need to identify relevant external facts
publication.limits: The account does not demonstrate determinism of a FinKore evaluation. A consistent evaluation does not certify the material truth of external information or establish exception policy.
